meaning: An ACL is a list of rules attached to a resource or network device that allows or denies specific users, addresses, or traffic.

meaning: AMD is a major maker of x86 processors and graphics cards, and its CPUs use sockets and chipsets different from Intel's.

meaning: An AUP is a written policy that defines how employees may and may not use company computers, networks, and internet access.

meaning: BNC is a twist-lock coaxial connector used for video equipment and older coaxial Ethernet networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A CLI lets a technician control a computer by typing text commands, such as in Command Prompt, PowerShell, or a Linux terminal.

source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: DB-9 is a nine-pin D-shaped connector used for RS-232 serial ports, commonly for console cables to network equipment.

meaning: DC is electrical current that flows in one direction, and it is the type of power a PC power supply delivers to internal components.

meaning: A PAN is a very small network, usually within a few meters, connecting personal devices such as phones, headsets, and watches via Bluetooth or NFC.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A PC is a general-purpose computer, such as a desktop or laptop, used by one person at a time and serviced by A+ technicians.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: PCI is an older parallel expansion bus that connects add-in cards like network and sound cards to a motherboard, replaced by PCIe.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: PCIe is the serial, lane-based expansion bus for graphics cards, NVMe drives, and other add-in cards, available in x1, x4, x8, and x16 slot sizes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: PCL is a page description language developed by HP that printers use to interpret print jobs and render text and graphics on the page.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists
note: The acronym list has "Printer Command Language"; objective 3.7 has "Printer Control Language". Both are accepted.

meaning: PHI is individual health information, such as medical records and billing details, that regulations like HIPAA require organizations to protect.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

meaning: PII is any data that can identify a person, such as a name, Social Security number, or address, and it must be protected from disclosure.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A PIN is a short numeric code that verifies a user locally, such as for unlocking a device or signing in with Windows Hello.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: PIV is a US government smart card standard that stores credentials and certificates for strong, multifactor identification of employees and contractors.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: PoE sends power and data over the same Ethernet cable, so access points, IP phones, and cameras need no separate power adapter.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: POP downloads email from a mail server to one client, used today as POP3 on TCP port 110, or 995 when secured.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: POST is the startup firmware check that tests essential hardware like RAM and the CPU, reporting failures through beep codes or error messages.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A PSU converts AC wall power into the lower DC voltages, such as 3.3, 5, and 12 volts, that computer components need.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A PUP is software a user may not want, such as bundled toolbars or adware, often installed alongside legitimate programs and hurting performance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: PXE lets a computer boot and install an operating system over the network using its network card, without any local drive or media.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: QoS settings prioritize certain network traffic, such as voice and video, so time-sensitive applications keep working smoothly when bandwidth is limited.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A QR code is a two-dimensional matrix barcode that a phone camera scans to open a link, join Wi-Fi, or enroll an authenticator app.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 5: Security Concepts

meaning: RADIUS is a protocol that provides centralized authentication, authorization, and accounting for network access, commonly used for enterprise Wi-Fi and VPN logins over UDP.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists
note: The official list has "Server"; the books and the RADIUS standard use Service. Both are accepted.

meaning: RAID combines multiple physical drives into one logical unit to improve speed, provide fault tolerance, or both, depending on the level used.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: RAM is the fast, volatile memory a computer uses to hold running programs and data, and its contents are lost when power is removed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: RDP is the Microsoft protocol that gives a user a remote graphical desktop session to another Windows computer over TCP port 3389.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: ReFS is a Microsoft file system designed for resilience and very large volumes, using checksums and self-healing, primarily on servers and Windows Pro for Workstations.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: RFID uses radio signals to read data from tags attached to objects or badges, commonly for access control, inventory tracking, and asset management.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: RGB is a color model that mixes red, green, and blue light at different intensities to produce the colors shown on displays and lighting.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: RISC is a processor design using a small set of simple instructions, as in ARM chips found in phones, tablets, and some laptops.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: RJ11 is a small connector with usually two or four wires, used for telephone lines and DSL modem connections.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: RJ45 is the eight-pin modular connector used on twisted-pair Ethernet cables to connect computers, switches, and routers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: RMM software lets managed service providers and IT staff remotely monitor, patch, and support many client computers from a central console.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: RPM measures how fast a hard drive's platters spin, with common speeds of 5400 and 7200, and higher values mean faster access.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: An RPS is a backup power supply, often used in servers, that automatically keeps the system running if the main power supply fails.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies

meaning: RSR is an Apple mechanism for delivering small, quick security fixes to iOS and macOS without a full operating system update.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: S.M.A.R.T. is a drive feature that monitors internal health indicators and warns of likely failure so data can be backed up in time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SaaS is a cloud model where users access finished applications, such as Microsoft 365, through a browser while the provider manages everything underneath.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SAE is the handshake used by WPA3-Personal that replaces the pre-shared key exchange and resists offline password-guessing attacks.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

meaning: SAML is an XML-based standard that lets an identity provider pass authentication assertions to other sites, enabling single sign-on across organizations.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists
note: The official list has "Assertions"; the books use Security Assertion Markup Language. Both are accepted.

meaning: A SAN is a dedicated high-speed network that gives servers block-level access to shared storage devices, typically using Fibre Channel or iSCSI.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SAS is a high-performance serial interface for enterprise hard drives and SSDs in servers, offering faster speeds and better reliability than SATA.
acceptedAnswers: Serial Attached Small Computer System Interface
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SATA is the standard serial interface connecting internal hard drives, SSDs, and optical drives to a motherboard, with SATA III reaching 6 Gbps.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SC is a square, push-pull fiber optic connector that snaps in place and is widely used on network equipment.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SCADA systems monitor and control industrial equipment such as power grids and factory machinery, and are a type of industrial control system needing special security.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SCSI is an older parallel interface standard for connecting hard drives and other devices, now largely replaced by SATA and SAS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SD is a small removable flash memory card format used in cameras, phones, and laptops, available in SD, SDHC, and SDXC capacities.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: An SDS provides details on a chemical's hazards, handling, storage, and first-aid and disposal measures, and technicians consult it for items like toner and batteries.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SFC is a Windows command-line tool, run as sfc /scannow, that scans protected system files and replaces corrupted ones with cached copies.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

meaning: SFTP transfers files securely over an encrypted SSH connection using TCP port 22, unlike plain FTP, which sends data in clear text.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A SIM is a small card that identifies a mobile subscriber to a cellular network and stores the account details for calls and data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: An SLA is a contract that defines the service level a provider must deliver, such as response times and uptime guarantees.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SMB is the protocol Windows uses to share files, folders, and printers over a network, running on TCP port 445.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SMS is the text messaging service on mobile networks, sometimes used to deliver one-time codes, though it is less secure than app-based methods.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SMTP is the protocol mail clients and servers use to send email, using TCP port 25 between servers and 587 for client submission.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SNMP lets administrators monitor and manage network devices such as routers, switches, and printers, using UDP port 161 for queries and 162 for traps.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

expanded: Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module
meaning: A SODIMM is a compact memory module used in laptops, mini PCs, and all-in-ones, physically smaller than the DIMMs found in desktops.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A SOHO is a very small business or home network, usually a few users sharing one router, and is the typical A+ configuration environment.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: An SOP is a documented set of step-by-step instructions that ensures a routine task is performed consistently and correctly every time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SPF is a DNS record that lists which mail servers may send email for a domain, helping receivers detect spoofed senders.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

expanded: Simple Protocol for Independent Computing Environments
meaning: SPICE is a remote display protocol used to access virtual machines, supporting features like audio, USB redirection, and clipboard sharing.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists
note: The Core 1 list has "Software Process Improvement and Capability Determination"; objective 220-1202 4.9 (remote access) and the books use the remote protocol meaning.

meaning: SQL is the standard language for querying and managing relational databases, and SQL injection attacks abuse it by inserting malicious statements into input fields.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: An SSD stores data on flash memory with no moving parts, making it faster, quieter, and more shock resistant than a mechanical hard drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SSH provides encrypted remote command-line access and secure file transfer to another system on TCP port 22, replacing insecure Telnet.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: An SSID is the name a wireless network broadcasts so users can identify and join it, and disabling the broadcast only hides it casually.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: SSO lets a user sign in once and access multiple applications without entering credentials again, reducing password fatigue while centralizing access control.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: ST is a bayonet-style fiber optic connector that twists and locks onto a port, used mostly in older multimode installations.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: STP is twisted-pair network cable with metallic shielding around the wires to reduce electromagnetic interference, used in electrically noisy environments.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals

meaning: TACACS, used today as TACACS+, centralizes authentication, authorization, and accounting for network device administration over TCP port 49.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that provides reliable, ordered delivery using acknowledgments and retransmissions, as used by web and email traffic.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: TKIP is an older encryption protocol introduced with WPA to improve on WEP, and it is deprecated in favor of AES with CCMP.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: TLS encrypts data in transit between clients and servers, such as HTTPS traffic on TCP port 443, and replaced the older SSL.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security

meaning: TN is an LCD panel type with fast response times and low cost, but it has narrow viewing angles and weaker color accuracy than IPS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: TOTP generates a temporary code from a shared secret and the current time, usually changing every 30 seconds, as authenticator apps do.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A TPM is a motherboard chip that stores encryption keys securely and supports features like BitLocker and Windows 11 security requirements.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A TXT is a DNS record type holding free-form text, commonly used to publish email authentication policies such as SPF and DKIM.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: UAC is a Windows feature that prompts for confirmation or administrator credentials before changes requiring elevated privileges, limiting what malware can do silently.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: UDP is a connectionless transport protocol that sends data without acknowledgments, making it fast and suited to streaming, VoIP, DNS, and DHCP.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: UEFI is the modern firmware that replaces BIOS, offering a graphical interface, Secure Boot, GPT disk support, and faster startup.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: UPnP lets networked devices automatically discover each other and open router ports, which is convenient but a security risk, so it is often disabled.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A UPS contains a battery that keeps equipment running briefly during an outage and conditions power, giving time for a safe shutdown.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: USB is the common interface for connecting peripherals and storage, with USB 2.0 at 480 Mbps and USB 3.x at 5 Gbps or more.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: USB-C is a small, reversible connector that can carry data, video, and power, used by modern phones, laptops, and Thunderbolt 3 and 4 ports.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A UTM device combines security functions like a firewall, intrusion prevention, antivirus, and content filtering into one appliance managed from a single point.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: UTP is common Ethernet cable with unshielded twisted wire pairs, in categories such as Cat 5e, Cat 6, and Cat 6a, with 100-meter runs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals

meaning: VA is an LCD panel type offering higher contrast and deeper blacks than IPS or TN, with viewing angles and response times in between.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: VDI hosts desktop operating systems on central servers and delivers them to users' devices remotely, simplifying management and keeping data off local machines.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: VGA is an older analog video standard and 15-pin connector, now largely replaced by digital interfaces like HDMI and DisplayPort.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A VLAN logically divides a switch into separate broadcast domains, so devices on different VLANs cannot communicate without a router.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A VM is a software-based computer that runs its own operating system on shared physical hardware, managed by a hypervisor.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: VNC lets a user view and control another computer's desktop over a network, using the RFB protocol and typically TCP port 5900.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists
note: The official list has "Computer"; the books use Virtual Network Computing. Both are accepted.

meaning: VoIP carries voice calls as data packets over an IP network, so it depends on adequate bandwidth, low latency, and QoS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel across an untrusted network such as the internet, letting remote users securely reach private resources.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: VRAM is dedicated memory on a graphics card that stores textures and frame data, with more capacity helping handle higher resolutions and complex graphics.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A WAN connects networks across large geographic areas, such as the internet linking separate offices, and is usually provided by a telecommunications carrier.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A WAP connects wireless devices to a wired network, creating a Wi-Fi network and often powered through PoE.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: WEP is an obsolete Wi-Fi security protocol with serious flaws that allow keys to be cracked quickly, so it should never be used.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: WinRM is a Windows service for remote management and PowerShell remoting, using HTTP on TCP port 5985 or HTTPS on 5986.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: A WISP provides internet access to customers over wireless radio links, which is common in rural areas where wired service is unavailable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists
note: The official list has "Written Internet Service Provider" (an error); objective 2.7 and the books use Wireless Internet Service Provider.

meaning: A WLAN links devices in a limited area using wireless radio signals, typically Wi-Fi based on the IEEE 802.11 standards.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: WPA is the Wi-Fi security standard that replaced WEP, using TKIP encryption and offering stronger protection than WEP.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: WPA2 secures Wi-Fi using AES encryption with CCMP, and it became the long-standing standard for personal and enterprise wireless networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware

meaning: WPA3 is the newest Wi-Fi security standard, using SAE for stronger password protection and improved encryption, including protection on open networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 46: Wireless Security and Malware

meaning: A WWAN provides wireless network connectivity over cellular networks, letting laptops and devices with a SIM or modem get internet access across wide areas.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: XaaS is a general term for any cloud service delivered on demand, covering models such as IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and others.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: XDR collects and correlates security data from endpoints, networks, email, and cloud sources so threats can be detected and handled across the whole environment.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: XFS is a high-performance journaling file system for Linux that handles very large files and volumes well, and it is the default on some distributions.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists

meaning: XSS is an attack that injects malicious script into a trusted web page so it runs in other users' browsers, often stealing session data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202) Exam Objectives – Acronym Lists
note: The Core 1 list has the typo "XXS".
